segments.narration: Everyone calls this an ancient battery, but archaeologists don't. One expert said she knew not a single colleague who believed it.
It came out of the ground in 1936 at Khujut Rabu, near the ruins of Ctesiphon.
The object is simple: a pot fifteen centimetres tall, a copper cylinder inside, an iron rod down the middle, sealed with bitumen.
In 1938 Wilhelm Konig said galvanic cell, maybe for plating gold onto silver. Fill it with something acidic and it does make current.
Replicas managed 4.33 volts on lemon juice. But no wires, no plated objects, and the pottery looks Sasanian. Most likely it held scrolls.
